hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger is redis-cache restarting at 07:40:07 after a node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#2228). Every /search product lookup then missed the cache. By 07:41:41 the search-api miss ratio was 96% against a 3% baseline, and each miss was loaded from catalog-db (#2372). That is a cache stampede onto the database. catalog-db went to 485/500 connections at 96% CPU (#2317), then 471/500 with too many clients (#2508). Single-id SELECTs on products slowed to 3.5-8s (#2414, #2902, #3276). search-api queries then timed out after 5s (#2410). web-bff 504s are a downstream symptom and are not cited. The notif-worker stack overflow (#2051) and metrics-agent exporter drops are unrelated to the search path. Redis itself stayed healthy with 0 errors. The restart is a small trigger; the damage comes from amplification.

catalog-db connection slots (500) and CPU were saturated. This is the database-side symptom of the cache stampede rather than the origin, so it is a weaker alternative. It would be the right category only if the connection limit were the true fault, but the timing follows the redis-cache restart, not an independent pool or CPU spike.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore or warm redis-cache (its snapshot was missing after node replacement; reseed or re-enable persistence). Add request coalescing or single-flight and rate limiting on cache-miss loads to catalog-db. Add catalog-db connection headroom. Alert on redis-cache restarts that come back with an empty keyspace. Confirm search p99 recovers as the hit rate returns to baseline.
